root_cause.text: ksmbd frees `oplock_info` with `kfree()` immediately after nullifying the pointer, without waiting for an RCU grace period, allowing concurrent RCU readers to access freed memory and cause a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The commit description states that "ksmbd currently frees oplock_info immediately using kfree(), even though it is accessed under RCU read-side critical sections ... Since there is no RCU grace period delay between nullifying the pointer and freeing the memory, a reader can still access oplock_info structure after it has been freed. This leads to a use-after-free." The patch replaces `kfree(opinfo)` with `call_rcu(&opinfo->rcu, free_opinfo_rcu)` to defer freeing until after an RCU grace period, and adds an `rcu_head` to the `oplock_info` struct.
